:::{#exm-evidence-lower-bound-decomposition}
#### The ELBO and the divergence for a three-valued latent variable

<!-- no-figure: the example is a table of three rows -->

Let $z$ take the values $1, 2, 3$ with [prior](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-prior) [probabilities](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $0.5, 0.3, 0.2$.
After the data $x$ is observed, its probabilities given $z$ are $0.1, 0.4, 0.8$.
The code below finds the [posterior](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-posterior),
then computes the [ELBO](#def-evidence-lower-bound) and the divergence for three choices of $q$,
with [natural logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-natural-log).

```{r}
#| label: evidence-lower-bound
prior <- c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2)
likelihood <- c(0.1, 0.4, 0.8)
joint <- prior * likelihood
evidence <- sum(joint)
posterior <- joint / evidence
log_evidence <- log(evidence)

elbo_and_divergence <- function(q) {
  log_ratio <- log(joint) - log(q)
  elbo <- sum(q * log_ratio)
  log_gap <- log(q) - log(posterior)
  divergence <- sum(q * log_gap)
  c(elbo = elbo, divergence = divergence, total = elbo + divergence)
}

uniform <- rep(1 / 3, 3)
shifted <- c(0.2, 0.3, 0.5)
rows <- rbind(
  uniform = elbo_and_divergence(uniform),
  shifted = elbo_and_divergence(shifted),
  posterior = elbo_and_divergence(posterior)
)
round(rows, 4)
```

The [evidence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-marginal-likelihood) is $`r evidence`$,
so its [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) is $`r round(log_evidence, 4)`$.
In every row the ELBO plus the divergence equals this value, as @thm-evidence-lower-bound-decomposition says.
The ELBO is largest, and the divergence is $0$, for $q$ equal to the posterior.

:::
